newsitem.title: USA: U.S. May single-family home sales rose 7.1 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. May single-family home sales rose 7.1 pct.

text.p: U.S. Commerce Department reported sales of new single-family homes, seasonally adjusted, with percent changes from prior month (numbers in 1,000s).
Total May sales of single-family homes rose 12.7 percent from an annualized rate of 732,000 units a year ago.
Note-Actual number of new single-family units sold is not seasonally adjusted.
Wall Street economists forecast May single-family home sales at a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 786,000 units.
The department also revised monthly percent changes of total sales, seasonally adjusted, from prior months as follows:
The annualized sales rate for February was revised to 826,000 units from 820,000.
Number of Months: Apr Mar-(Prev) Feb-(Prev)
The monthly increase in total new home sales for May was the largest since an 11.6 percent rise in November 1996.
The number of months' supply at the current sales rate for May was the lowest since March 1971 when it was 4.0 months. In addition, the number was matched at 4.1 months in July 1971.
The number of homes for sale in May was the lowest since July 1993, when the level was 278,000.
The sales rate for homes in the Midwest in May was the highest since January 1996, when it was up 31.7 percent.
